steps.body: You can measure length by counting how many small objects fit end to end — like paperclips. A pencil that's 5 paperclips long is longer than an eraser that's 3 paperclips long. More units means longer.
Measure a pencil by iterating paperclip-sized units.

widget.prompt: Measure the pencil. Align zero, use one-paperclip units, and cover it with five units exactly.
widget.successFeedback: Five equal paperclip units cover the pencil exactly, so its length is 5 paperclips.
widget.alignFeedback: Start the first unit at the pencil’s starting end.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Every paperclip unit must touch the next without gaps or overlaps.
widget.unitFeedback: Use one-paperclip units so the count is in paperclips.

cml.actionGoal: Iterate a nonstandard unit and connect coverage count to length.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Change the unit size while measuring the same object. What changes, and what physical quantity stays fixed?

explanation.prompt: Why is the final ruler label not always the object’s length?

options.label: Length is the distance between start and end, not the end label alone.
options.feedback: Exactly — subtract the start or iterate units across the interval.

options.label: The end label always equals the length.
options.feedback: That works only when the object starts at zero.

predict.prompt: What must be true when units measure length?

options.label: Equal units touch end to end from the object’s start.
The ending ruler label is always the length.

predict.reveal: Measurement iterates equal units from the correct starting point with no gaps or overlaps.

steps.body: The same idea tells you which is shorter — just look for the smaller count. Fewer units means shorter, the same way more units means longer.

widget.prompt: A book is 8 blocks long. A phone is 3 blocks long. Tap the SHORTER one.

items.label: book
items.feedback: The book is 8 blocks long — more than the phone's 3. The phone is shorter.

widget.missFeedback: Fewer stripes means shorter — the phone, at 3, is shorter.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 3 blocks is fewer than 8, so the phone is shorter.

steps.body: Always compare with the same unit. If a pencil is measured in paperclips and an eraser is measured in cubes, you can't compare their counts directly — the units have to match.

widget.prompt: A spoon is 6 cubes long. A fork is 9 cubes long. Tap the longer one.

items.feedback: The spoon is only 6 cubes long. The fork, at 9, is longer.

widget.missFeedback: Count the stripes: 9 beats 6 — the fork is longer.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 9 cubes is more than 6, so the fork is longer.

steps.body: Measuring with the same unit lets you compare lengths by comparing counts.
takeaways: More units of length means longer.
Only compare counts measured in the same unit.

concept.body: When two objects are measured in the same unit (like paperclips), the one with the bigger count is longer. A pencil at 5 paperclips is longer than an eraser at 3.

explanationVariants: 5 is more than 3, so the pencil is longer.

widget.prompt: A pencil is 5 paperclips long. An eraser is 3 paperclips long. Which is longer, the pencil or the eraser?

options.label: the eraser
options.feedback: 3 is fewer than 5; the pencil is longer.
